findings.source_quote: οὕτως π[ερὶ θεοῦ] ἢ οὐ τὰ ἀνθρώποις προσόντα λέγειν καὶ σιωπᾶν ἔστιν ἢ τῶν ἀνθρώποις προσόντων κα[λῶν] εὖλογόν ἐστιν ἀπονέμειν αὐτῷ τὰ κ[ρείτ]τονα
findings.english_quote: Thus, concerning God, either one cannot speak of the qualities belonging to human beings and must remain silent, or it is reasonable to assign to him the better of the good qualities belonging to human beings.
findings.issue: The draft turns refraining from speech into inability to speak and adds an obligation to remain silent. The construction defensibly permits ἔστιν to govern the coordinated infinitives οὐ ... λέγειν καὶ σιωπᾶν: it is possible not to speak of these attributes and to remain silent. This reading also fits the contrast with reasonably assigning the better attributes. The note does not preserve this material alternative; its alternative instead places the negation over possibility itself.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review: “Thus, concerning God, either one may refrain from speaking of the qualities belonging to human beings and remain silent, or it is reasonable to assign to him the better of the good qualities belonging to human beings.” Explain the compressed coordination and distinguish this reading from a wider scope for οὐ.

findings.source_quote: τὸ πονηρὸν ἑτέρα τις ἐγέννησεν ἀρχὴ ἢ ἄρ’ ἀγέννητόν ἐστιν; καὶ ὁ Πέτρος Οὔτε ἑτέρα τις δύναμις ἐγέννησεν τὸν πονηρὸν οὔτε ἀγέννητόν ἐστιν τὸ κακόν
findings.english_quote: some other first principle begot the evil one, or that he is perhaps unbegotten?
findings.issue: Simon uses the neuter τὸ πονηρὸν and ἀγέννητον, whereas Peter subsequently uses the masculine τὸν πονηρὸν and then the neuter τὸ κακόν. Rendering Simon’s expression as “the evil one” and “he” silently removes this observable transition between evil and its personal embodiment. The following context makes a personal interpretation defensible, but the draft supplies no comparison with “evil” or explanation of that choice.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, render Simon’s wording “some other first principle begot evil, or that it is perhaps unbegotten?” while retaining Peter’s “the evil one” and “evil.” Alternatively, submit an explicit note preserving the neuter wording, the alternative “evil,” and the contextual reason for the personal rendering; do not treat that proposed disclosure as already accepted.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὡς μεγάλα κυματουμένη τῷ διδασκάλῳ πλέοντι καὶ γαλήνην ἐπιτάξαντι τάχιστα πεισθεῖσα ἡσύχασε;
findings.english_quote: And when it surged into great waves while the Teacher was sailing, then quickly obeyed when he commanded calm and became quiet?
findings.issue: This is further evidence attached to the preceding rhetorical question about matter fearing the stronger, parallel to its acknowledgment through earthquakes. The draft turns that evidentiary continuation into an unfinished, freestanding “And when ...?” question. The events survive, but their rhetorical and syntactic relationship is obscured.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep this clause attached to the preceding question, for example: “...as it also acknowledges by trembling through earthquakes, and as, while surging in great waves, it at once obeyed the Teacher, who was sailing and commanded calm, and became quiet?” Submit the revised sentence for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὢν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;
findings.english_quote: does he not himself exist as the cause of evils while this matter gives birth?
findings.issue: The proposed analysis does not establish a defensible connection between the masculine nominative participle ὢν, ἐστιν, and the intervening finite clause αὕτη τίκτει. “Exist as” does not by itself resolve that construction, and “while” supplies an attendant relationship that the note asserts without demonstrating. The note acknowledges irregularity and the conjecture ὧν, but then presents the unsupported attendant-clause analysis as a nonblocking resolution. The block concerns unresolved meaning in surviving, verified wording—not an alleged OCR error and not merely the existence of alternative interpretations. The five- and six-dot lacunae elsewhere are explicitly retained and adequately disclosed, so they do not cause this selected-edition coverage block.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a demonstrable grammatical analysis of the supplied ὢν construction, or textual and philological support for an explicitly identified correction. The proposed correction “οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὧν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;” would support “is he not himself the cause of the evils that this matter begets?”, but it is not the supplied reading and is not an accepted replacement. Any resulting English and disclosure require fresh review; further verification of the already image-checked print alone would not resolve the meaning.
